candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate interdisciplinary and telehealth resources, arrange consultation and transfer, and use systems that improve access to timely care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telestroke consultation and transfer coordination
candidate.educational_objective: Use telestroke as a systems-of-care resource that brings remote stroke expertise to hospitals without on-site specialists and supports rapid imaging interpretation, reperfusion decisions, and transfer planning while local clinicians continue hands-on care.

options.A: It gives the local team rapid remote access to stroke expertise and imaging review to support thrombolysis, triage, and transfer decisions when on-site specialists are unavailable.
options.B: It replaces all in-person nursing, emergency, radiology, and follow-up care for the remainder of the hospitalization.
options.C: It is useful mainly in large academic centers and offers little benefit to remote hospitals without local neurologists.
options.D: It should be used only after reperfusion-treatment decisions are complete because telemedicine has little role in acute stroke evaluation.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline states that telestroke bridges gaps in access to stroke expertise, particularly in remote locations. In the emergency setting, telestroke and teleradiology support timely review of brain imaging, thrombolytic decision-making, and triage or transfer for endovascular thrombectomy when appropriate. B overstates telemedicine as a replacement for local hands-on care. C reverses its equity/access purpose. D is incorrect because acute treatment decisions are a central telestroke use.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Telestroke provides remote specialist consultation and imaging-based decision support for acute stroke, improving access to timely thrombolysis and transfer/triage decisions in hospitals lacking on-site stroke expertise.
candidate.source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
candidate.source_locator: Section 2.8 Telemedicine — Synopsis: telestroke bridges access gaps for remote patients; in acute ED care, teleradiology/telestroke enable timely brain-imaging review, thrombolytic decision-making, and timely treatment. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text: telestroke supports hospitals without on-site neurological expertise and can aid triage/transfer for EVT or allow appropriate local care.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
candidate.stem: A rural hospital without an on-site stroke neurologist activates its telestroke system for a client with suspected acute ischemic stroke. What is the main benefit of this system?
